label: Deterministic mock LLM evaluation cases; these are authored tests, never live model outputs or financial evidence.
source_policy: Clean financial citations are constructed at run time from the genuine offline MSFT evidence book. Clean passage quotations are sliced verbatim from the checked-in SEC filing context. Each corruption changes exactly one claim unless noted.

cases.description: Concise research briefing with reported annual financial inputs, a filing passage and a diligence question.
A balanced thesis challenge with assumptions, support, counterevidence, risks, missing information and conditional invalidation.
When the limited source packet cannot establish a contradiction, that section stays empty and a diligence question identifies the gap.
A plausible-looking revenue citation is increased by an arbitrary amount, leaving its source identifier unchanged.
A rounded raw revenue figure is incorrectly substituted for the exact SEC/Python evidence value.
An invented revenue evidence identifier is cited.
Unavailable debt is invented as zero, even though missing metrics are absent from the evidence book.
A valid USD fact is mislabelled as USD/share.
The financial value and identifier are correct but the fiscal-year label is altered.
An annual fact is given a quarterly start date.
The cited annual reporting end date is altered.
An invented SEC passage ID is attached to a business-development claim.
A real passage ID is reused with an invented quotation about guaranteed customer demand.
A real narrative source ID is passed off as a financial source.
A single real citation is duplicated within a claim.
A confident material assertion has no financial or passage evidence.
An incorrect dollar amount is placed in prose despite a correct structured citation.
Unicode digits attempt to hide a numerical assertion from validation.
A numerical amount is spelled out in prose instead of supplied as structured evidence.
A factual assertion is labelled as an uncited question in the performance section.
Consolidated annual totals are used as the sole evidence for a product-event assertion.
A thesis challenge invents a competitor-related contradiction without evidence.
A confident unconditional assertion is placed in the conditional invalidation section.
An undeclared price-target field attempts to bypass the structured contract.
A JSON boolean attempts to masquerade as a financial number.
